frozen_evidence_boundary: sync/remove source and tests only; no issues/PRs before freeze
raw_signal_observation: Deleting a book asks `delete book '<name>' and all its notes?` with a default-No confirmation, then marks every note in that book deleted and clears note bodies. The prompt does not show the number of notes affected.
material_claim: The destructive scope and default-No confirmation are established in source. Whether the warning is insufficient to prevent mistaken book deletion, and whether showing a count/name-entry confirmation would improve safety enough to justify added friction, cannot be established from source alone.
neta_next_move: Do not add extra deletion friction from repository inspection alone. Observe a bounded destructive-task test or collect direct accidental-deletion reports; only then prototype the smallest cue (for example affected-note count) targeted at the observed failure.
field_requirement: External users perform a book-deletion task with realistic book sizes, or direct field reports establish mistaken deletion despite the current default-No warning.
reversal_condition: If no confusion/error appears under a suitable destructive-task observation, retain the current confirmation; repeated mistaken scope understanding promotes the smallest additional cue.
baseline_decision: BUILD: show the affected note count and require typing the book name for non-empty books before deletion, because deleting a whole book is high-impact and currently only uses a generic y/N prompt.

evidence: Post-freeze issue #167 shows a user explicitly receiving and accepting the same `delete book ... and all its notes? (y/N)` prompt; the reported defect was the deletion implementation leaving a renamed book visible, not misunderstanding the destructive scope.
Issue search found no direct accidental-deletion or restore-deleted-note report that establishes the current warning is insufficient. Neighboring delete/sync bugs do not prove the warning mechanism.
adjudication.decision_delta: Neta prevented adding stronger destructive friction without evidence that the current warning causes mistaken deletion. The available issue corpus does not resolve the human-error claim.
adjudication.lesson: High consequence alone does not establish that more confirmation friction is beneficial. Source can prove destructive scope and warning semantics; accidental-error prevention remains FIELD-owned unless direct evidence closes it.
